title: BottomUpRolloutVerdict
description: One judge's evidence-grounded verdict on one agent rollout. The ONLY fixed classification is outcome_class (TP/TN/FP/FN); everything else is open free-text grounded in cited evidence, kept deliberately free of any failure taxonomy so it can be clustered downstream.

citation.description: A precise, machine-readable pointer into one artifact. Exactly one of two shapes, so a viewer can jump to the cited step(s) or highlight the cited line range.

steps.description: Precise trajectory step index/indices the claim rests on (0-indexed steps in trial/trajectory.json).

quote.description: Short verbatim snippet from those step(s).

file.description: Artifact path ('task/…' or 'trial/…', e.g. 'task/solution/solve.sh', 'trial/test_stdout.txt') OR a live-workspace absolute path (e.g. '/testbed/src/foo.py').

line_end.description: Inclusive end line; == line_start for a single line.

verifier_signal.description: Echoed verbatim from result.json — the verifier's machine verdict, the 'given'. binary_reward is the PASS(1)/FAIL(0) gate.

judge_verdict.description: The judge's INDEPENDENT assessment, against task intent + reference solution.

task_truly_solved.description: Did the agent genuinely accomplish what the task asked, as the reference solution would recognize — independent of whether the tests passed?

summary.description: One short plain sentence for list views — the bottom line of what happened (no footnotes needed). The full grounded judgment goes in outcome_rationale.

outcome_class.description: verifier signal x truth. TP: pass & solved. TN: fail & not-solved. FP: pass & NOT solved (spurious pass / weak verifier). FN: fail & solved (spurious fail / broken task).

outcome_rationale.description: The COMPLETE judgment as ONE cohesive paragraph (no line breaks, headers, or bullets). Open with a crisp characterization of the verdict (e.g. 'This was a genuine agent-fault failure — the verifier's FAIL is correct.'), then flow through what the verifier did/reported, what the task required, what the agent actually did/produced, and why this is the right TP/TN/FP/FN — with inline footnote(s) [N] grounding every factual claim in the numbered evidence. For FP/FN (claims the verifier is wrong) be concrete: name the gap between what the tests check and what the task/reference require, or the harness/format/env failure.

evidence.description: Grounded claims. Each claim carries >=1 machine-readable citation pinning precise trajectory step(s) or a file line-range. The summary / rationale must be backed here.

claim.description: A specific, load-bearing factual statement, footnoted from the summary/rationale by its 1-based position in this list.

verifier_or_task_concern.description: null if the task + verifier look sound. Otherwise a grounded note on why the verifier or task itself appears at fault (over-strict, gameable, ambiguous spec, broken environment) — feeds the separate broken-task / patch workflow. Typically non-null exactly when outcome_class is FP or FN.
